title: Scoring a cleaning audit: room, element and area percentages
audience: Cleaning supervisors and auditors who score audits or prepare audit reports in healthcare facilities
learningOutcomes: Calculate a room percentage from element scores
Calculate a functional area average from room percentages
Check a published total before relying on it

instruction.heading: The room score
instruction.body: Each element scores 1 if it is acceptable and 0 when it fails. Elements that are not present in a room are left out of the count. The room percentage is acceptable points divided by achievable points, multiplied by 100. A room with 45 acceptable points against 50 achievable scores 90 per cent.

instruction.heading: The area score
instruction.body: An area's score is the average of its room scores. Average the room percentages, not the raw points, so that rooms with different numbers of applicable elements count equally.

instruction.heading: Check the arithmetic before you publish
instruction.body: Totals can be wrong. The Irish manual's worked example lists six room scores, listed in order as seventy, sixty, sixty-five, seventy, ninety and sixty-five and prints a total of 430. Those values actually add to 420, and their average is 70 per cent. The printed total, and the 71 per cent that followed from it, are therefore wrong. Always re-add the values yourself, and correct any sheet that does not add up before it is saved or reported.

instruction.heading: Recording the result
instruction.body: Record each failed element with its reason and a time for action. Report the area score together with the number of rooms it was calculated from, so that a later reader can check the figure.

procedure: Score each element 1 or 0, and mark absent elements as not applicable.
Add the acceptable scores and the achievable scores for each room.
Convert each room to a percentage.
Average the room percentages for the area.
Re-add the values and check the total before saving the sheet.

workedExamples.situation: A surgical area has rooms scoring seventy, sixty, sixty-five, seventy, ninety and sixty-five. The sheet prints a total of 430.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the correct area score?
workedExamples.reasoning: The room values add to 420, so the average is 70 per cent. The printed 430 is an addition error. Correct the sheet and note the correction, so the area score is not reported from the wrong total.

commonErrors.error: Averaging raw points instead of room percentages
commonErrors.prevention: Convert each room to a percentage, then average those percentages.

commonErrors.error: Copying a printed total without re-adding the values

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Irish numbers are used here only to illustrate the method. For SA facilities, the SA audit scoring and pass levels govern (see “Internal audits: how often each area is audited and the pass mark”).
